summary_paragraph: A woman with Hb-SS disease was admitted for worsening pain and swelling in her left shin following repeated trauma. Imaging revealed a deep soft tissue abscess with signs of tibial osteomyelitis, including cortical thinning and bone marrow edema, despite negative blood and fluid cultures. A CT-guided bone biopsy was performed, with initial gram stain showing no organisms or white blood cells; cultures remained pending at discharge. Vancomycin was initially given but stopped due to red man syndrome and to optimize culture yield. The patient was clinically stable with controlled pain and no signs of acute sickle crisis. She was discharged home on her baseline medications with plans for close follow-up with infectious disease and orthopedics to determine need for surgical intervention or antibiotic therapy based on final biopsy results.
